title: Objects, colors, and describing things
objectives: Describe things with ma- adjectives (malaki, maliit, maganda...)
Join describing words to nouns with the linker na / -ng
Name everyday objects and their colors, and ask Ano ang kulay...?

grammar.title: Adjectives with ma-
grammar.explanation:
Most Tagalog adjectives are built from a root plus the prefix ma-: ganda (beauty) gives maganda (beautiful), laki (size) gives malaki (big), init (heat) gives mainit (hot). Once you spot this pattern, new adjectives become easy to learn in pairs: malaki/maliit (big/small), mainit/malamig (hot/cold), malinis/marumi (clean/dirty), bago/luma (new/old — these two happen to have no ma-).

Using an adjective is simple because there is no word for 'is': adjective first, topic second. Malaki ang bahay — 'The house is big.' Maganda si Ana — 'Ana is beautiful.' Masaya ako — 'I'm happy.' You've been doing this since Mabuti ako in Unit 1.

To exclaim, use ang + the adjective (you saw Ang sarap! in Unit 4): Ang ganda! 'How beautiful!' Ang laki ng bahay nila! 'Their house is so big!'

grammar.title: The linker na / -ng
grammar.explanation:
When an adjective sits right next to its noun ('a big house', 'cold water'), Tagalog glues them together with a linker. The rule has three cases. If the describing word ends in a vowel, attach -ng directly: malaki → malaking bahay (big house), pula → pulang bag (red bag). If it ends in n, that n becomes ng: ulan → maulang araw (rainy day). If it ends in any other consonant, leave the word alone and put the separate word na after it: maliit na bahay (small house), malamig na tubig (cold water).

The order can flip freely: malaking bahay and bahay na malaki both mean 'big house'. Flipping doesn't change the meaning, only the emphasis a little.

You already know this glue from numbers (dalawang pusa, isang kape) and from walang + noun. It's everywhere in Tagalog — whenever two words describe each other, expect a linker between them.

examples.tl: Gusto ko ng mainit na kape.

grammar.title: Plural with mga; asking about color
grammar.explanation:
To make a noun plural, put mga (pronounced ma-NGA) before it: ang mga bata — 'the children'; mga libro — 'books'. The noun itself never changes shape. Don't double up: with a number, skip mga — tatlong libro, not tatlong mga libro.

Colors work like other describing words and take the linker: pulang bag (red bag), itim na sapatos (black shoes). To ask a color: Ano ang kulay ng bag mo? — 'What color is your bag?' Answer: Pula. or Pula ang bag ko.

Note how the ng marker earns its keep again: kulay ng bag = 'color OF the bag'. The ang/ng team from Units 3–4 runs through everything you'll say.

examples.tl: Ano ang kulay ng damit niya? — Dilaw.
examples.en: What color is her dress? — Yellow.

examples.tl: Itim na sapatos ang gusto ko.
examples.en: Black shoes are what I want.

example.en: May I have a pencil, please.

example.tl: Ano ang kulay ng bag mo?
Itim na bag ang bag ko.
example.en: My bag is a black bag.

vocab.note: Bughaw is the deep-Tagalog word, rarer in speech

example.tl: Maliit na bahay ang bahay nila.
example.en: Their house is a small house.

example.tl: Gusto ko ng malamig na tubig.

vocab.note: Pronounced 'ma-NGA'; skip it when a number is present

example.tl: Maliit ang bahay namin pero malinis.
example.en: Our house is small but clean.

dialogue.title: Whose bag is this?
dialogue.context: After class, three bags are left on the table. Ben helps Kate find hers.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: Kate, ito ba ang bag mo?

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.tl: Hindi. Itim ang bag ko. Asul iyan.
lines.en: No. My bag is black. That one's blue.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: Ay, oo nga. Malaki ba o maliit ang bag mo?
lines.en: Oh, right. Is your bag big or small?

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.tl: Maliit na itim na bag. May pulang susi sa loob.
lines.en: A small black bag. There's a red key inside.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: Iyon ba, ang itim na bag sa mesa?
lines.en: Is it that one, the black bag on the table?

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.en: Yes! That's the one! Thanks, Ben.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: Walang anuman. Ang ganda ng bag mo, ha. Bago ba?
lines.en: You're welcome. Your bag is really nice, huh. Is it new?

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.tl: Hindi, luma na ito. Pero paborito ko ito.
lines.en: No, it's old now. But it's my favorite.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: May mga libro ka ba sa bag? Ang bigat!
lines.en: Do you have books in the bag? It's so heavy!

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.tl: Oo, may tatlong libro at isang malaking payong.
lines.en: Yes, there are three books and one big umbrella.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: Tatlong libro! Masaya ang klase mo, ha!
lines.en: Three books! Your class must be fun, huh!

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.tl: Masaya, pero mahaba. Sige, salamat ulit!
lines.en: It's fun, but long. Okay, thanks again!

exercises.prompt: Which prefix builds most Tagalog adjectives, as in maganda and malaki?
exercises.explain: Ma- attaches to a root: ganda (beauty) → maganda, laki (size) → malaki.
Malaki ends in a vowel, so the linker -ng attaches directly: malaking bahay. (Bahay na malaki is also fine.)

exercises.prompt: Gusto ko ng malamig ___ tubig. (I want cold water.)
exercises.explain: Malamig ends in the consonant g, so the linker is the separate word na: malamig na tubig.

exercises.prompt: What is the opposite of malinis (clean)?
exercises.explain: Marumi means dirty — the pair is malinis/marumi, like mainit/malamig and malaki/maliit.

exercises.prompt: Bago ang ___ libro namin. (Our books are new — plural)
exercises.explain: Mga before a noun makes it plural: mga libro = books.

exercises.tl: Ano ang kulay ng bag mo? — Itim, at may pulang susi sa loob.
exercises.prompt: What color is the bag, and what is inside?
choices: Red bag with a black key
Black bag with a red key
Blue bag with a yellow key
White bag with a red pen
exercises.explain: Itim = black answers the color question, and pulang susi = a red key (pula + linker -ng).

exercises.prompt: Which is the correct way to say 'three chairs'?
exercises.explain: With a number you use the linker (tatlong) but drop mga — number and mga don't combine.

exercises.prompt: My watch is old (a thing, not a person): ___ na ang relo ko.
exercises.explain: Luma is 'old' for objects; matanda is 'old' for people.

exercises.prompt: Her dress is beautiful. It is yellow.
exercises.answer: Maganda ang damit niya. Dilaw ito.
accept: Maganda ang damit niya. Dilaw ito
Maganda ang damit niya. Dilaw iyon
Maganda ang damit niya, dilaw ito
exercises.explain: Adjective first, topic second: Maganda ang damit niya; then Dilaw ito states the color with no word for 'is'.

exercises.tl: Maliit ang bahay namin pero malinis at masaya.
exercises.prompt: How does the speaker describe their house?
exercises.explain: Maliit = small, pero = but, malinis = clean, masaya = happy/cheerful.

exercises.prompt: Gusto ko ng mainit na kape at dalawang bagong pandesal.
exercises.answer: I want hot coffee and two new pandesal.
accept: I want hot coffee and two new pandesal
I'd like hot coffee and two fresh bread rolls
I want hot coffee and two fresh pandesal
I would like hot coffee and two new bread rolls
exercises.explain: Mainit na kape = hot coffee (linker na after a consonant), dalawang bagong pandesal chains two linkers: two + new + pandesal.

exercises.prompt: The chairs are small, but the table is big.
exercises.answer: Maliit ang mga silya, pero malaki ang mesa.
accept: Maliit ang mga silya pero malaki ang mesa
Maliliit ang mga silya, pero malaki ang mesa
Maliit ang mga silya, pero malaki ang mesa
exercises.explain: Mga pluralizes silya; each clause is adjective + ang + noun, joined by pero (but).

exercises.prompt: You want to exclaim 'How beautiful!' about a friend's new watch. What do you say?
exercises.explain: Ang + bare root makes an exclamation: Ang ganda! — like Ang sarap! from the food unit.
